core_obligations: Set up the induction on k and dispose of the cases k = 0, 1 (proof lines 2294-2297).
Write the Koszul-type exact complex and derive from it the first quadrant spectral sequence converging to the homology of Sym^k(F) (proof lines 2298-2314).
Apply the Eilenberg-Zilber lemma to identify the E_1 terms as derived tensor products (proof lines 2315-2321).
Conclude using the induction hypothesis and the vanishing of H_0 of the wedge powers, which follows because they are quotients of tensor powers of F (proof lines 2322-2329).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: in the setting of the punctual topos with a cosimplicial object as in the resolution lemma, a flat B-module F with H_0(C, F) = 0 satisfies H_l(C, Sym^k(F)) = 0 for l < k (source lines 2281-2292). The proof is an induction on k built on the Koszul-type exact complex whose terms are wedge powers tensored with symmetric powers: viewing it as a resolution of Sym^k(F) produces a first quadrant spectral sequence converging to the homology of Sym^k(F), the Eilenberg-Zilber lemma rewrites the derived lower shriek of each term as a derived tensor product of two derived lower shrieks, and the induction hypothesis together with the vanishing of H_0 of the wedge powers (a quotient of F^{tensor q+1}) gives the claim.
